holidays.name: National Coffee Day
holidays.description: A caffeinated celebration for java lovers in the United States, often marked by free or discounted cups at coffee shops and a collective excuse to have one more cup. Other countries mark International Coffee Day on October 1, so September 29 gives Americans a head start.
holidays.origin: National Coffee Day has been observed in the U.S. on September 29 for years, popularized by coffee chains and food-holiday calendars. It grew out of promotional events and a general national devotion to caffeine.
holidays.funFact: Legend says coffee was discovered by an Ethiopian goat herder named Kaldi, who noticed his goats dancing around after eating berries from a certain bush.

holidays.name: Confucius's Birthday (Teachers' Day in Taiwan)
holidays.description: A day honoring the famed Chinese philosopher Confucius, celebrated with ceremonies, traditional music, dance, and rituals. In Taiwan it doubles as Teacher's Day, when students express gratitude to their educators.
holidays.origin: Confucius is traditionally said to have been born on September 28 or 29 in 551 BCE. Taiwan's government set the observance in the 20th century to honor teaching and the sage's legacy, with ceremonies held at Confucian temples.
holidays.funFact: At Confucian temple ceremonies in Taiwan, ritual dancers perform with ceremonial props like feather and flute, in a style believed to be centuries old.

holidays.name: Michaelmas
holidays.description: A traditional Christian feast day honoring the Archangel Michael and all angels, once a major date in the English calendar. It was one of the quarter days when rents were due, servants were hired, and new magistrates were elected.
holidays.origin: Michaelmas dates back to the early church and was widely celebrated in medieval Europe. It marked the end of the harvest and the start of autumn, and was linked to folk customs such as eating goose.
holidays.funFact: English folklore says that blackberries should not be picked after Michaelmas because the Devil, cast out of heaven by Michael, fell into a bramble bush, spat on it, and cursed the fruit.

holidays.name: World Heart Day
holidays.description: A global awareness day encouraging people to look after their tickers by eating well, exercising, and quitting smoking. Expect health walks, free blood pressure checks, and plenty of heart-shaped everything.
holidays.origin: Founded in 2000 by the World Heart Federation in partnership with the World Health Organization and UNESCO. It was originally held on the last Sunday of September, and in 2014 it was fixed to September 29.
holidays.funFact: Your heart beats around 100,000 times a day, pumping roughly 2,000 gallons of blood through your body.

holidays.name: Vermont Maple Syrup Fan Day Adjacent: National Attend Your Grandchild's Birthday Isn't It... Actually: Ask a Stupid Question Day Alternative: International Day of Awareness of Food Loss and Waste
holidays.description: A United Nations observance urging people to cut down on food that is lost in supply chains or tossed in the trash. It encourages everything from smarter shopping to using up those sad leftovers hiding in the back of the fridge.
holidays.origin: The UN General Assembly established it in 2019, with the first observance in 2020, to boost efforts toward reducing global food waste as part of the Sustainable Development Goals.
holidays.funFact: The UN estimates that roughly a third of all food produced for human consumption is lost or wasted each year.
